# User Manual — FleetPulse

**For:** fleet operators, dispatchers and maintenance staff
**Written for a non-technical reader.** If you are installing the system rather than using
it, read `docs/07-installation-guide.md` first.
**Generated by AI prompt:** P-20.

---

## 1. What FleetPulse does

FleetPulse watches every vehicle in your fleet — buses and delivery trucks — and tells you
the moment something goes wrong. Each vehicle reports its position and its sensors every
few seconds. FleetPulse checks each report against your operating rules and raises an
**alert** when a rule is broken.

It does not drive anything, dispatch anything or contact drivers. It tells you, quickly,
what needs your attention.

---

## 2. Opening the dashboard

Go to <http://localhost:5173> in your browser.

At the top left is the FleetPulse name. At the top right is the **connection indicator** —
read it before you trust anything else on the screen:

| Indicator | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **● live (ws)** | Data is arriving the instant it is produced. Normal. |
| **● polling (ws down)** | The live connection dropped. The screen still updates, every 5 seconds, and reconnects on its own. |
| **● connecting…** | Starting up. |

If the indicator is not green, your screen may be up to five seconds behind reality.

---

## 3. The Fleet Overview screen

### 3.1 The four tiles

| Tile | Read it as |
|---|---|
| **Vehicles** | How many vehicles exist, and how many are currently reporting |
| **Critical** | Problems that need action now |
| **Warnings** | Problems to keep an eye on |
| **Offline** | Vehicles that have gone silent |

If Critical and Offline are both zero, nothing needs you right now.

### 3.2 The map

Every reporting vehicle is drawn on the map:

- **Circle** = bus, **square** = truck
- **Solid line** = bus route, **dashed line** = truck route, **small dot** = a timetabled stop
- The marker's colour and the label beside it show that vehicle's state

Click any vehicle to open its detail page.

### 3.3 The alert feed

The list on the right shows every open alert, **worst first**. Each card tells you:

- the severity — with an icon and a word, not only a colour
- which vehicle
- what is wrong, in plain language, with the measured value and the limit it broke
- **×3** — how many times this same problem has repeated. One ongoing fault stays as one
  card with a rising counter, rather than flooding the screen.

Two buttons on each card:

- **Acknowledge** — "I have seen this and I am handling it." The alert leaves the open feed
  and your team can see it is being worked.
- **Resolve** — "This is finished." The alert is closed and the vehicle's state improves.

You may resolve directly without acknowledging first. You cannot re-open a resolved alert —
if the fault happens again, FleetPulse raises a fresh alert, so the history stays honest.

### 3.4 The vehicle table

Everything the map shows, plus the numbers, sorted worst-first. Use the **all / bus /
truck** buttons to narrow it down.

The table deliberately stops re-sorting while your mouse is over it, so a row never moves
out from under your click.

---

## 4. Vehicle states

| Shown as | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **● ok** | Reporting normally, no open alerts | Nothing |
| **ⓘ info** | Advisory only | Note it |
| **⚠ warn** | An open warning | Plan a response |
| **⛔ crit** | An open critical alert | Act now |
| **○ offline** | No report within the timeout, or the vehicle is in maintenance / retired | Check whether it is a breakdown or a tracker fault |

---

## 5. What each alert means

| Alert | It means | Typical response |
|---|---|---|
| **OVERSPEED** | Faster than the route's posted limit, beyond the allowed tolerance | Contact the driver; review if repeated |
| **ENGINE_OVERHEAT** | Engine temperature above the warning (or critical) limit | Critical: instruct the driver to stop safely |
| **LOW_FUEL** | Fuel below the low (or critical) level | Route to a fuel stop |
| **ROUTE_DEVIATION** | Outside the permitted corridor around its route | Check for a detour, a wrong turn, or theft |
| **VEHICLE_OFFLINE** | Nothing heard for longer than the timeout | Call the driver; if unreachable, treat as a possible breakdown |
| **HARSH_BRAKING** | A large speed drop between two consecutive reports | Driver-behaviour and near-miss review |
| **SCHEDULE_DELAY** *(buses)* | Projected to reach its next stop later than the timetable allows | Consider a relief bus or a timetable adjustment |
| **CARGO_TEMP_EXCURSION** *(trucks)* | The refrigerated load is outside its permitted temperature band | Act quickly — the load may be at risk |

`SCHEDULE_DELAY` is only ever raised for buses and `CARGO_TEMP_EXCURSION` only for trucks.

---

## 6. The vehicle detail page

Click a vehicle anywhere — map, table or alert card — to open it.

- **Top strip** — current speed, engine temperature, fuel, cargo temperature (trucks) and
  when the vehicle last reported.
- **Charts** — the last 60 readings. The dashed lines across the charts are the thresholds,
  so you can see how close a value is to breaking a rule, not just where it is now. A
  temperature line climbing towards the dashed critical line is a breakdown you still have
  time to prevent.
- **Alert history** — every alert this vehicle has raised, open and closed.

Press **← Back to fleet** to return.

---

## 7. The Alert Centre

The overview feed shows what is open now. The Alert Centre shows **everything**, including
resolved alerts, and lets you filter by:

- **Status** — open, acknowledged or resolved
- **Severity** — critical, warning or info
- **Vehicle** — e.g. `BUS-03`
- **Rule** — e.g. `OVERSPEED`

Use it for end-of-shift review ("what happened while I was away") and for investigating a
particular vehicle's pattern.

---

## 8. Settings — tuning the rules

Open **Settings** to change any threshold. Changes take effect on the very next reading;
nothing needs restarting.

| Setting | Raise it to… | Lower it to… |
|---|---|---|
| Overspeed tolerance | Get fewer speeding alerts | Enforce limits more strictly |
| Engine warning / critical | Reduce noise from an older fleet | Get earlier mechanical warnings |
| Fuel low / critical | Warn earlier about fuel | Warn only when nearly empty |
| Harsh braking Δ | Report only severe braking | Catch gentler braking events |
| Heartbeat timeout | Tolerate patchy mobile coverage | Detect silent vehicles sooner |
| Schedule grace (buses) | Accept more lateness | Enforce the timetable tightly |
| Alert cooldown | Fewer repeat alerts, higher counters | More separate alerts for one fault |

Two combinations are rejected because they would make a rule unreachable: the engine
critical value must be **above** the warning value, and the fuel critical value must be
**below** the low value.

**Reset defaults** restores everything.

> Tuning tip: if the same alert appears constantly for the whole fleet, the threshold is
> probably wrong for your vehicles, not the fleet. If it appears for one vehicle, the
> vehicle probably has a real problem.

---

## 9. Keyboard and accessibility

- Every table row and map marker can be reached with `Tab` and opened with `Enter`.
- Severity is shown as an icon **and** a word as well as a colour, so the screen is
  readable without colour vision and in greyscale print.
- The alert feed is announced to screen readers as new alerts arrive.
- The brief highlight on a new alert is disabled automatically if your system is set to
  reduce motion.

---

## 10. Common questions

**Why is the same problem only one alert?**
An ongoing fault would otherwise produce one alert every few seconds. FleetPulse groups
repeats of the same rule on the same vehicle into a single alert and counts them (**×n**).
A genuinely new occurrence, after the fault has been quiet, gets its own alert.

**Why did an alert say "warning" and later "critical"?**
Severity increases if the situation worsens. It never decreases on its own — once an
operator has seen "critical", it stays critical until it is resolved.

**Why does an offline vehicle's alert close by itself?**
Because the vehicle started reporting again — that is directly observable, so FleetPulse
closes it for you. No other alert type closes automatically.

**A vehicle is in the workshop and keeps alerting.**
Set its status to `maintenance`. Its readings are still stored but no rules are applied.

**Are the numbers on a closed alert still trustworthy after old data is cleaned up?**
Yes. Each alert stores the measured value and the limit it broke at the moment it fired, so
it remains fully readable long after the underlying telemetry has been pruned.
